title: Risk Assessment of an Illegal Laboratory in Reedley, California, Using Geospatial Analysis of Open‐Source Epidemic Intelligence Data

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to estimate epidemic signals around the Reedley illegal laboratory using open-source epidemic intelligence data. The Gi * value is classified on the basis of the outbreak signals in the US or California: hotspots (a higher number of signals than expected), cold spots (a lower number of signals than expected), and nonsignificant (with comparable numbers of observed and expected outbreak signals), based on 90%, 95%, and 99% confidence intervals (Ord and Getis 2010).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used geospatial analysis of open-source epidemic intelligence data for California and the US from October 2021 to October 2023. Search terms included all possible pathogens mentioned at the Reedley illegal laboratory (The Select Committee 2023; Nava 2023).
analysis.methods: The spatial pattern of outbreak signals was analyzed using hotspot analysis, and the distances of outbreak signals from the laboratory were measured. Data curation, processing, and cleaning utilized R tidyverse packages and MS Excel; graphs were made using ggplot, and maps were made using ArcGIS. We analyzed the trends of pathogens documented in the illegal laboratory, along with those not documented in the illegal laboratory in the US and California, to compare trends within and across each category.
analysis.main_results: Of the 19,233 outbreak signals reported in the study period, 33.3% were country-level reports without state-level location data, 25.2% were state-level reports, and 41.5% were finer than the state level (Figure 1). In the period after the establishment of the Reedley illegal laboratory in October 2022, reported outbreaks of pathogens associated with the illegal laboratory showed a slight increase in December 2022, June to August 2023, and October 2023 across the US (Figure 2). The nearest outbreak signals from the Reedley illegal laboratory are ∼41 and 33 km away, before and after the illegal laboratory started operating, respectively (Figure 5).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The October 2023 increase in reports of disease due to pathogens associated with the laboratory is temporally related to locally acquired cases of dengue being reported in California in late 2023 (California Department of Public Health 2025, Sutter-Yuba Mosquito and Vector Control District 2025). Changes in disease patterns reported in California or the US in the year following the establishment of the illegal laboratory may or may not be linked to the illegal laboratory.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Early warning systems, such as EPIWATCH, have the potential to detect unusual outbreaks of infectious disease much sooner than traditional surveillance methods, and when formal data are unavailable. The availability of open-source data does not depend on whether a laboratory incident has been formally reported to domestic or international authorities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In the absence of any formal testing, reporting or data, but knowing that a staff member and their child became ill, we have shown that EPIWATCH can be used to analyze whether any unusual epidemic patterns were reported in the area. The supplied evidence does not report any formal testing or data to confirm a causal link between the illegal laboratory and the observed disease patterns.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to estimate epidemic signals around the Reedley illegal laboratory using open-source epidemic intelligence data. It analyzed the spatial patterns of outbreak signals and compared trends of pathogens associated with the illegal laboratory to those not associated. The results showed that 33.3% of outbreak signals were country-level reports, while 41.5% were more granular. There was a slight increase in outbreaks of pathogens linked to the illegal laboratory in specific months, and the nearest outbreak signals were approximately 41 and 33 km away. However, the study acknowledges that the observed changes in disease patterns may not be directly linked to the illegal laboratory. The findings highlight the potential of EPIWATCH for early detection of unusual outbreaks, even in the absence of formal data. The study's limitations include the lack of formal testing and the possibility of other factors influencing the reported disease patterns.

title: Respiratory pathogens detected by multiplex PCR in Malaysian public hospitals: prevalence and epidemiologic patterns from January 2023 until July 2024.

analysis.research_question_and_background: We aimed to describe the prevalence, demographic associations, and temporal trends of respiratory pathogens detected by the QIAstat-Dx Respiratory SARS-CoV-2 Panel in Malaysian public hospitals.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This multicentre retrospective cross-sectional study included nasopharyngeal swab samples from cases with suspected acute respiratory infections tested between 1 January 2023 and 31 July 2024.
analysis.methods: Data were collected from participating sites using standardised record forms and analysed.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Respiratory tract infections remain an important cause of hospitalisation and diagnostic uncertainty, and multiplex polymerase chain reaction testing offers rapid detection of multiple pathogens in routine clinical practice.

analysis.summary_en: We aimed to describe the prevalence, demographic associations, and temporal trends of respiratory pathogens detected by the QIAstat-Dx Respiratory SARS-CoV-2 Panel in Malaysian public hospitals. This multicentre retrospective cross-sectional study included nasopharyngeal swab samples from cases with suspected acute respiratory infections tested between 1 January 2023 and 31 July 2024. Data were collected from participating sites using standardised record forms and analysed. The leading pathogens also demonstrated distinct temporal profiles, with different peak months across the study period. In conclusion, respiratory pathogen detection in this hospital-based population was characterised by a high positivity rate, predominance of viral pathogens, marked age-related differences, and distinct temporal patterns. Respiratory tract infections remain an important cause of hospitalisation and diagnostic uncertainty, and multiplex polymerase chain reaction testing offers rapid detection of multiple pathogens in routine clinical practice. Positivity was highest among children aged 1 to 4 years and infants aged 1 to 11 months, and age-related variation was more pronounced than regional variation.

title: A digitalized nosocomial risk management framework during the COVID-19 pandemic: practice-based insights from a tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a digitalized nosocomial risk management framework in preventing SARS-CoV-2 transmission within a tertiary cancer hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic, given the heightened vulnerability of cancer patients to infection and mortality.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a single-center case study conducted at a tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China over a 32-month period, focusing on the implementation of a digitalized risk management program during the national Zero-COVID policy period.
analysis.methods: The program utilized a digital risk-reporting pipeline built on Questionnaire Star® and R programming language, incorporating systematic integration of management strategies with digital technologies, and relied on community-level non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) such as lockdowns, mass testing, and travel restrictions.
analysis.main_results: Over the 32-month study period, the hospital achieved a 98% staff vaccination rate with 95% booster coverage. No nosocomial COVID-19 cases were detected among patients or staff during the surveillance period. The program was reconfigured within 48 hours to address other infectious diseases such as influenza.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the absence of detected nosocomial cases as an association rather than proof of causation, noting that the program's effectiveness may have been influenced by concurrent community-level restrictions. The novelty lies in demonstrating the utility of integrated, multi-component infection prevention strategies using digital tools.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that systematic integration of management innovations with digital technologies can support hospital infection prevention during outbreaks, particularly in high-risk settings like cancer hospitals, and highlight the importance of such frameworks for post-pandemic preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-center design, which restricts generalizability, and the concurrent community-level restrictions that may have confounded the assessment of the program's standalone effectiveness. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates a digitalized nosocomial risk management framework implemented at a tertiary cancer hospital in Southwest China during the COVID-19 pandemic. The framework integrated management strategies with digital technologies, including a Questionnaire Star®-based surveillance system and R programming language. Over 32 months, the hospital achieved a high staff vaccination rate and did not detect any nosocomial COVID-19 cases, despite repeated community outbreaks. The authors interpret these results as an association rather than proof of causation, given the concurrent national Zero-COVID policy. The study highlights the potential of integrated, multi-component infection prevention strategies for high-risk settings and post-pandemic preparedness. However, its single-center design limits generalizability, and further multi-center studies are needed to validate the framework's effectiveness. The findings suggest that digital tools can support hospital infection prevention, but their standalone impact remains unclear due to overlapping public health measures.
